result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returning `await fetch(...)` — a raw Response — when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, while in HubspotCalendarService the result is annotated and consumed as `HubspotToken` (the parsed object from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken`). In sync mode the code will then treat a Response (no accessToken/expiresIn fields) as the token and write it into credential.key, corrupting the HubSpot credential. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: The refreshed value is annotated and consumed as HubspotToken (an object with accessToken etc. from hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken), but in sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, which is then used downstream as if it were the parsed token. With credential sync enabled, HubSpot's credential update writes a serialized Response object (or undefined token fields) into credential.key, corrupting the HubSpot integration the next time it is used.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a raw `Response` object. But in `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is awaited and assigned to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = ...`, where the non-sync path returns the HubSpot SDK token object (`hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`). With sync enabled, downstream HubSpot code will receive a `Response` instead of a `HubspotToken`, so accesses like `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` / expiry fields (and any subsequent credential update using that object) will be incorrect and can corrupt stored credentials or break refresh logic.
